extracted.intended_audience: Contracting Officers and procurement personnel (primarily U.S. Navy/DoD) implementing OMB Circular A-76 (CITA program)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for Contracting Officers to plan, execute and administer Commercial Industrial Type Activities (CITA) contracting under OMB Circular A-76, including the cost-comparison process, Phase I assessment activities, acquisition planning/solicitation/evaluation, and contract administration considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost comparison process (sequence & responsibilities)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sequence of steps for conducting an A-76 cost comparison from Task Group establishment through award/cancellation, including roles of Approving Authority (AA), Independent Auditor (IA), Task Group (TG), Prospective Contractor (PC), and Contracting Officer (CO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps depicted: Establish Task Group; Establish Schedule/Prepare SOW (TG); Review SOW (GO); Prepare/Audit In-house Cost Estimate (TG/IA); Issue Solicitation (CO); Submit Sealed In-house Cost Estimate (TG); Submit Bids/Proposals (PC); Determine Low 'Contract Price' (CO); Conduct Cost Comparison (IEE); Complete/Certify Cost Comparison (MTG/IA); Prepare Decision Summary/Recommendations (TG); Approval (AA); Public Review (CO); Conduct Pre-award survey (CO) if private industry cost appears lower; Announce results to general public and allow time for review; upon completion either award contract or cancel solicitation. Responsibilities and audit/pre-award survey steps emphasized; Task Group certifies cost comparison and Approving Authority makes final decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-phase framework (Assessment, Acquisition, Administration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall framework dividing the CITA implementation into Phase I (Assessment of Commercial Industrial Type Activities), Phase II (Acquisition — Planning and Contracting), and Phase III (Contract Administration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phase I is ongoing until determination made about retention in-house; Phase II overlays the cost comparison and contains pre-solicitation, solicitation/evaluation, and award cycles; Phase III begins at award and continues through contractor performance. Use framework to identify issues affecting the Contracting Officer beyond the narrow cost comparison process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase I activity: Preparation of the C/I inventory
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare the Commercial/Industrial (C/I) inventory of functions under review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventory preparation is a typical Phase I activity and the starting point for determining which functions may be subject to review or conversion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase I activity: Establishment of review schedules
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish schedules for reviewing functions in the inventory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review schedules drive fiscal-year planning and coordination; once identified, functions are difficult to move between years (Congress is advised of the inventory schedule).

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase I activity: Justification for in-house performance based on National Defense
rubrics_metrics.description: Document and justify retention of functions in-house where national defense considerations require it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National Defense can be a basis for in-house performance; documentation should support this justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase I activity: Justification for in-house performance based on non-availability of commercial sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare justification and documentation when claiming no satisfactory commercial source is available to perform the function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensive substantiation is required, including documentation that existing firms lack sufficient capacity or technical competence; agency must make requirement known broadly (see CBD notice requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase I activity: Preparation of and submission of fact sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare fact sheets describing the function and supporting data for review/decision-making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fact sheets support the assessment and provide standardized information for Task Group and higher authority review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase I activity: Grouping of similar type functions for possible solicitation packages
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider grouping similar functions into consolidated solicitation packages to attract larger, experienced firms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grouping can reduce combined price, solicitation and administration costs, and centralize management; coordination and standardized work statements are necessary for success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase I activity: Consideration of multifunctional solicitations (umbrella contracts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the use of multifunctional or 'umbrella' contracts (e.g., Base Operation Support Service) to cover many base services under a single contractor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advantages: potential lower overall price, reduced solicitation/admin costs, centralized management. Disadvantages: turbulent phase-in/turnover, coordination/start-up problems, complex conversion issues. Contracting Officer's role is advisory in grouping functions; manpower limits may constrain efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase I activity: Determination of core capability requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify core capabilities that must be retained or required from contractors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination of core capability informs solicitation design, performance standards, and what must remain in-house.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase I activity: Preparation of local implementing directives
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop local implementing directives to guide CITA implementation at the field level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local directives provide consistent execution and must align with higher-level policy and inventory schedules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase I activity: Exploring utilization of excess capacity at other Government agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider use of excess capacity at other federal agencies as an alternative to contracting out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exploring intra-governmental options may be part of assessing commercial availability and cost-effective solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase I activity: Communications with interested parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Manage communications with unions, private industry, Congress, media, and other stakeholders during assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications are sensitive; Contracting Officer must avoid indicating decisions reserved to higher authority and coordinate FOIA responses with legal counsel and higher authority as needed. Replies to union inquiries should be consistent and coordinated with Naval Supply Systems Command.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of availability of commercial sources (CBD notice requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before retaining a function in-house for non-availability of commercial sources, the agency must make the requirement known to a broad cross-section of American industry, including Commerce Business Daily (CBD) notices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimum CBD requirement: at least three notices over a 90-day period; for urgent requirements, two notices over a 30-day period. Also obtain assistance from GSA, SBA and similar agencies. The CBD notice need not state it is under the Circular, and replies need only indicate availability (not proof of capability), though the guidance questions whether evidence of capability should be requested. Even one commercial source might preclude in-house retention if literally interpreted. Priced informational solicitations are unacceptable as the basis for a lower in-house cost exception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and limits of informational solicitations and market surveys
rubrics_metrics.description: Informational solicitations and market surveys may be used to gauge commercial interest but have disadvantages and are insufficient alone to establish non-availability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disadvantages: contractors may not invest time/expense on information-only responses; responses may be low quality; they may not reach all potential sources. Market surveys (e.g., via SBA) helpful but do not guarantee broad notice. CBD notices plus agency assistance required; priced informational solicitations cannot be the basis for lower in-house cost exception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidation of same functions across activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Standardize and centralize review schedules and consolidate identical function requirements across multiple activities to produce coordinated solicitation packages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benefits include coordinated work statements and a single large contract (reported satisfactory for janitorial consolidation in San Diego). Barriers include lack of coordination, varying work statements quality, policies promoting small/disadvantaged business participation that may conflict with consolidation, and centralized schedule decisions at higher HQ that limit local flexibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardized work statement quality and coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure work statements submitted by activities for the same service are consistent and of acceptable quality to enable consolidation or large solicitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observed variation from acceptable to poor among submitted work statements; lack of similarity hinders consolidation. Contracting Officer participation or leadership in planning can improve coordination and standardization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications with interested groups and FOIA handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Handle inquiries from unions, media, Congress, and FOIA requests carefully, coordinating with legal counsel and higher authority where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responses (e.g., lengthy FOIA questionnaires) should be supported by documentation and coordinated with legal counsel. Avoid statements that imply final decisions; coordinate union replies with Naval Supply Systems Command; field activities retain responsibility for public inquiries but should seek higher-level advice as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase II planning issues (internal organizational considerations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Address internal organizational matters prior to solicitation: workload impacts, staffing, training, Procurement Administrative Lead Time (PALT), and contracting authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advance planning and procurement personnel availability are critical; activities should review internal organization, staffing and workload to implement policy guidelines effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role in Task Group and input to SOW/milestone planning
rubrics_metrics.description: As a member of the Task Group, the Contracting Officer provides inputs to Statement of Work (SOW) development and milestone planning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting Officer attention in Task Group affects scheduling, SOW content, and integrity of the cost-comparison process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation and contracting considerations (methods, sources, clauses, contract type, options)
rubrics_metrics.description: During contracting, address methods of solicitation, sources of supply (including small/disadvantaged businesses), DAR coverage, appropriate clauses, determination of contract type, and use of options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These items may require increased pre-solicitation review. Special clauses (e.g., Service Contract Act) and selection of contract type and options impact administration and future performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation/evaluation cycle practices (conferences, negotiations, competition philosophy, evaluation methodology)
rubrics_metrics.description: Manage pre-bid/pre-proposal conferences, re-examine negotiation methods given the Government may be an offeror, clarify competition philosophies, and adopt revised proposal evaluation methodologies (including incentive arrangements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-bid/proposal conferences may require closer attention; negotiation approaches must account for a government in-house offerer; evaluation methodologies and incentive structures may need revision to ensure fair comparison and competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award cycle considerations (evaluation vs award factors, in-house estimate timing, public announcements, protests/appeals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Differentiate between evaluation and award factors; address late submission of Government in-house cost estimates and the correct timing to reveal the estimate; understand preliminary/final announcement requirements and public review periods; be aware of discrepancies arising from verification/audit and understand appeals vs protest procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting personnel must grasp requirements for announcements and public review, and handle appeals/protests appropriately when discrepancies surface from cost verification/audits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service contract-specific requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize special requirements for service-type contracts: ensure services are non-personal, include Service Contract Act clauses on wages/fringe benefits, craft longer/more complex SOWs, provide contractor performance measurement provisions, and plan site visits if work on Government facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service contracts are generally more complex than supply contracts and require special clauses, performance metrics, possible options for extensions, and safeguards to avoid employer-employee relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase III contract administration considerations (surveillance, performance standards, delegation, phase-in)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan for contract administration: establish surveillance plans, define performance standards linked to SOWs, decide on delegation of contract administration (e.g., DCAS), and manage phase-in/turnover milestones during conversion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contract administration starts at award and continues through contractor performance; some administration may be delegated but limitations exist (DCAS limited role); phase-in issues may be complex for multifunction conversions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational/staffing models and resource planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether existing contracting office organization and staffing are adequate to implement CITA actions; consider models (cradle-to-grave vs separate contract administration branches), need for COTA/COTRs/QAEs, and possible creation of CITA coordinators or billets at activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Field activities reported understaffing; options include creating dedicated CITA coordinators, assigning procurement series personnel at activities to support SOW prep and admin, and training requirements. Additional positions are more likely to be assigned at activity receiving services rather than the contracting office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on delegation to Defense Contract Administration Services (DCAS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize DCAS may provide limited support on CITA service contracts; contracting offices often rely on original negotiator for complex administration issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except for limited tasks (e.g., wage negotiation), DCAS may be of little help with significant CITA contract administration problems; plan staffing accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to add 4% to contractor bid/offer for Government contract administration cost estimate
rubrics_metrics.description: When computing probable Government cost for contract administration in comparisons, add 4% to the contractor's bid or offer to indicate Government contract administration costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This adjustment is used in the cost comparison to reflect Government administration burden; contracting offices should apply this as part of cost analysis.
